acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: One shared predicate decides the gate, and both cmd_dispatch_check and dispatchable_task_ids consult it.
A high/critical task whose contract is registered on the remote default branch and unchanged on the seven governance fields is dispatchable on both surfaces.
A high/critical task whose contract is absent from, or diverges from, the remote default branch is refused on both surfaces, with a named reason.
The comparison is over exactly mergegate_check._NORMAL_PATH_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS, imported rather than redeclared, so the immutability gate and the dispatch gate cannot drift.
The gate fails closed: when registration cannot be verified, it refuses instead of dispatching.
Low and medium risk keep dispatching from local state, without consulting the remote.
A binder test proves both surfaces agree on the same task in both the admit and the refuse case, and fails if either surface is changed without the other.

SADR-0015's "What shipped, and when." paragraph stops claiming the pre-dispatch gate shipped 2026-07-27 through 2026-07-29, records that it was deferred there as an explicit non-goal, and records where it actually shipped.
The full Python suite, validate_shiki, and the dispatch-exercising shell suites stay green.
CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.

decisions: The gate is absent from both code paths, measured not inferred. cmd_dispatch_check (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:1189,1198) sets guardian_required from risk_level and appends "guardian approval required for high/critical risk" unconditionally, with no branch that can clear it; dispatchable_task_ids (scripts/shiki_runtime.py:236) never reads risk_level at all (grep -c risk_level scripts/shiki_runtime.py == 0). shiki_loop.py's four risk_level uses are all merge-time (auto-merge eligibility at :349 and :473), never dispatch-time. Live reproduction: T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54 is risk high, its contract is present at origin/main, and dispatch check still returns the blocker.

It was deferred, never descoped. T-20260727T005125902419Z-6c2db440 — the task that delivered the registration half in the 2026-07-27..29 window SADR-0015 credits — carries "The pre-dispatch gate or the envelope ceiling" as an explicit non_goal, and its source plan P-20260727T005119007135Z-1fa476be repeats it. No later Goal picked the gate up. Unlike the Scope Envelope ceiling, which G-20260801T040836630398Z-f28167e5 descoped on the record, no descope record exists for the gate. The remedy is therefore to implement it, and to correct a shipped-claim that was never true — not to descope.

The shared predicate lives in scripts/shiki_tasks.py beside evaluate_lock_grant. This is the precedent set by T-20260805T034218808409Z-0f0d9640 ("Make a granted lock a precondition of dispatch"), which solved the same drift between the same two surfaces: shiki_runtime.py already imports from shiki_tasks, so no import cycle is introduced, and no new module means no scripts/shiki_installer.py manifest entry and no tests/test_install_completeness.py change.

The seven governance fields are imported from mergegate_check._NORMAL_PATH_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS, never redeclared — the single-constant discipline scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py already documents, so the fields a PR may not change are exactly the fields the gate compares. Measured: none of mergegate_check's imports (shiki_contracts, shiki_evidence, shiki_guardian, shiki_jsonschema, shiki_locks, shiki_manifest, shiki_schema) reference shiki_tasks, so the import forms no cycle.

Governance-fields-only comparison is load-bearing, and the measurement confirms SADR-0015's reasoning. try_acquire_locks flips status to "ready" and appends a lock ledger id before dispatch, while a registered contract is still "planned": measured 2026-08-24, 14 of the 19 non-done high/critical tasks are status "planned" on origin/main. A whole-file comparison could never succeed and would leave the gate permanently closed.

Blast radius is zero today. Simulating the gate against live state: all 19 non-done high/critical tasks have their contract on origin/main, and all 19 show zero drift across the seven fields, so the gate would admit every one of them and block none. Enforcing it now costs no in-flight work.

Lock sufficiency was measured, not estimated. A throwaway prototype of the predicate and both call sites was applied in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46 and then reverted: the full Python suite (1185 tests), validate_shiki, and the module_boundaries, control_plane, run_orchestrator, daemon_runner, loop_lock_guard, goal_loop and runner_claude shell suites all stayed green. No existing test binds either surface's current behaviour — which is exactly why the two could drift, and why the binder test is the missing pairing rather than an extra.

The prototype also proved the satisfaction path the CLI has never had: with the gate applied, dispatch check on T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54 drops the guardian blocker entirely and returns only its outstanding lock blocker.

The record correction is a second, dependent task. The corrected paragraph asserts that the gate shipped, which is true only once the code lands, and separating it isolates the docs/adr/SADR-0015 lock — which collides with the in-flight descope task T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54. Both tasks are status planned, so the collision is a serialization point, not a present conflict.

docs/agents/decision-control.md belongs to the code task, not the record task. Its Dispatch Guard section prints the exact shape cmd_dispatch_check emits and states "If any field is false, the runtime must not edit files"; the gate changes that shape and retires guardian_approval_required as a blocking field. Its lock collides with critical task T-20260822T102714799429Z-c43ccdcf, also planned — again a serialization point. decision-control.md:61 ("risk level does not require unresolved Guardian approval") already states the requirement and becomes true when this lands, so its wording needs no change.

scripts/shiki_tasks.py collides with five planned tasks (T-20260822T095306178275Z-0dc8a0b4, T-20260801T041653424169Z-07860c35, T-20260822T095306177744Z-38bafdfb, T-20260801T041653348713Z-6283adcd, T-20260822T095306176491Z-a152348c). It is a central module and lock serialization is the intended mechanism; none holds an active grant today.
grill_with_docs.source: Requirements Definition 2026-08-24 in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46, driven by an operator report and confirmed by direct measurement against the repository rather than by design review.

non_goals: Modifying evaluate_guardian_approval or any of its four existing approval sources. The pre-dispatch gate is a dispatch precondition, not an approval source.
Changing the merge-time Contract Approval carry (shiki_contract_approval.evaluate_contract_approval) or either of its two consumers. That half shipped 2026-08-01 and is out of scope.
Implementing the Scope Envelope size ceiling. It is a frozen non-goal of G-20260801T040836630398Z-f28167e5 and its descope record is owned by G-20260822T103718385731Z-f0b5eff6.
Editing CONTEXT.md. Its Scope Envelope entry belongs to the in-flight descope task T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54, which holds that lock.
Rewriting SADR-0015's Context section. It records the problem as it stood at decision time and stays as history; only the shipped-record claim is corrected.
Changing how risk_level is resolved anywhere, or lowering any task's risk.
Changing the Contract PR path, contract mode, goal_reconcile, or task registration.

Backfilling or re-registering contracts for existing tasks. Measured 2026-08-24: all 19 non-done high/critical tasks already carry their contract on origin/main with zero governance-field drift, so the gate admits all 19 and no backfill is needed.

Authoring a spec_freeze block, Guardian approval evidence, a CCA verdict, or any other approval record. Approval is reserved to its authority (AGENTS.md Approval Records). An acceptance criterion that cannot be satisfied with the artifacts present in the worktree must be reported as a stop, never closed by manufacturing the missing artifact.
outcome: A high/critical task is dispatchable only when its contract is registered on the remote default branch and agrees with local state on the seven frozen governance fields, decided once by a shared predicate that BOTH the advertised surface (shiki_runtime.dispatchable_task_ids) and the CLI readiness surface (shiki_tasks.cmd_dispatch_check) consult, so the advertised and enforced sets cannot drift. Measured 2026-08-24 in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46: `grep -c risk_level scripts/shiki_runtime.py` returns 0, and `shiki dispatch check T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54` returns "guardian approval required for high/critical risk" as a blocker with no satisfaction path even though that task's contract is present at origin/main (registered by Guardian-approved Contract PR #341, merge commit 2d7a193). SADR-0015's "What shipped, and when." paragraph therefore claims a gate that no code path implements, and the record is corrected to say what actually happened.
title: Enforce the SADR-0015 pre-dispatch gate on both dispatch surfaces
